items.title: Ox Hill Battlefield sits inside later development
items.now: A small county park holds the Fairfax ground of the 1862 fight.
items.place: This was the Chantilly battlefield. Homes and roads later covered most of the field.
items.change: The park footprint is what remains of that battlefield in a built landscape.

items.title: Accotink Creek is under a long restoration plan
items.now: County work is changing stream banks, ponds, and trail edges in this basin.
items.place: Accotink Creek drains parks, neighborhoods, and older mill land to the Potomac.
items.change: Restoration changes where water moves and which banks stay planted.

items.title: East Potomac Park is under National Park Service review
items.now: NPS manages this filled river park, golf course, and cherry planting.
items.place: The land is a historic recreational landscape on the Potomac.
items.change: Park plans can shift the golf, paths, and tree layout on the same footprint.

items.title: Manassas battlefield still meets new roads and lots
items.now: The national battlefield holds the core of First and Second Manassas.
items.place: Two Civil War battles were fought on this Bull Run ground.
items.change: Park lines show what is protected next to later roads and houses.

items.title: Scotts Run gorge is a protected stream corridor
items.now: The county park keeps the gorge trail and stream banks open to walkers.
items.place: Scotts Run drops through a rocky corridor to the Potomac.
items.change: Park rules keep the banks planted and keep climbers off rare rock plants.
